**Continuous 2.36.0**, a community-maintained fork of the Continue VS Code extension. Continuous is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Continue Dev, Inc.

It installs alongside the original extension (its ID is `b1tninja.continuous`), brings your existing `~/.continue` configuration with it, and collects no telemetry. To update from 2.34.0, 2.32.0, 2.30.0, 2.28.0, 2.26.0, 2.24.0, 2.22.0, 2.20.0, 2.18.0, 2.16.3, 2.16.2, 2.16.1, 2.16.0, 2.14.0, 2.12.x, 2.10.x or 2.4.x, install the new `.vsix` the same way, or let the Marketplace update it. Coming from 2.4.1 or earlier, also see [Continued is now Continuous](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/tag/v2.4.2-vscode) in the 2.4.2 notes: the extension ID changed.

## Install

1. Download the `.vsix` for your platform below and, optionally, check it against `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
2. Run `code --install-extension continuous-<platform>-2.36.0.vsix --force`, or in VS Code use the Extensions view: `...` → **Install from VSIX…**, then reload the window.

Requires VS Code 1.105 or newer. The packages are not code-signed. Full instructions: [install guide](https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/blob/main/docs/continuous-install.md). Continuous is also on the VS Code Marketplace as **Continuous** (`b1tninja.continuous`).

| Platform                    | File                                                                       |
| --------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Windows x64 / Arm64         | `continuous-win32-x64-2.36.0.vsix`, `continuous-win32-arm64-2.36.0.vsix`   |
| macOS Apple Silicon / Intel | `continuous-darwin-arm64-2.36.0.vsix`, `continuous-darwin-x64-2.36.0.vsix` |
| Linux x64 / Arm64           | `continuous-linux-x64-2.36.0.vsix`, `continuous-linux-arm64-2.36.0.vsix`   |

Each platform also has an **agents** build, `continuous-<platform>-2.36.0-agents.vsix`. It adds Continuous to VS Code's Agents window through APIs that are still proposed, so it works in VS Code Insiders, or in Stable started with `code --enable-proposed-api b1tninja.continuous`. Without that it works like the normal build. See [VS Code Chat and Agents](https://b1tninja.github.io/continuous/customize/vscode-chat-and-agents).

## The CLI

The terminal agent is attached as `continuous-cli-2.36.0.tgz`. Install it on Node 22 or newer:

```sh
npm i -g https://github.com/b1tninja/continuous/releases/download/v2.36.0-vscode/continuous-cli-2.36.0.tgz
```

The package is `@b1tninja/continuous-cli` and the command is `continuous` (`continuous serve` is the headless server; the notes below call it `cn serve` where the docs do). The short command `cn` also works; both run the same program. It reads the same `~/.continuous` configuration as the extension.

## What's new since 2.34.0

This is the warning release for headless fetches. `cn -p` and `cn serve` still fetch public hosts, and the notice now says that follows your Web level from 2.38, so the release that introduces the notice is not the one that changes the behaviour. Web is its own permission area. Safety checks are a choice: they stay on below IDGAF, and they stay off at IDGAF until you turn them on. Choosing "Read it for this model" after a leaked tool call now saves on a catalog model.

No new host is contacted by the extension or the terminal agent.

### New

- Web is a policy area of its own, with seven levels: Off, Manual, Cautious, Listed (only domains you allowed, never asks), Automatic, Permissive and IDGAF. Set it with `levels.web` in `permissions.yaml`, or in `cn` with `--policy web=<level>` (for example `--policy tools=permissive,web=listed`). Until you set it, Web follows Tool use, so the levels you saved keep their meaning. The presets set it too: Careful and Accept edits give Cautious, Hands off Permissive, Reviewer Automatic, IDGAF IDGAF; Off and Listed make the preset read Custom.
- At Cautious, a fetch runs without asking when you allowed its host: a `host:` rule in the `allow:` list of your `permissions.yaml` (`host:docs.example.com`, or `host:*.example.com` for the subdomains, matched on whole labels), a domain in your `trustedDomains`, an allow rule, the host allowed for this session, or the exact URL you wrote in your message. There is no built-in list of allowed hosts.
- `cn` asks about a fetch with **Allow `<host>` for this session**, **Always allow `<host>`** (adds `host:<host>` to your `permissions.yaml`) and **No**.
- `levels.web: off` refuses the agent's web tools (fetch and search; `cn` stops offering them) and leaves `@url` working. `web.enabled: false` in any config.yaml, a project's included, turns off every web fetch: the agent's tools, `@url` and the docs crawler. Only your own config.yaml can turn it back on.
- The headless start-up line of `cn -p` and `cn serve` names the Web level and what happens to a fetch there, for example `Web Cautious (unattended: public hosts still run in this release; from 2.38 only allowed domains)`.
- A shield beside the session controls turns safety checks on or off, and lists each built-in check so one of them can be switched on its own. The choice is saved in `permissions.yaml` as `safetyChecks: on` or `safetyChecks: off`. Leave it unset and the checks stay on, and stay off at IDGAF.
- A blocked call in Recently blocked has **Disable this rule** when that block came from one of those checks.

### Behaviour changes

- In interactive `cn`, `Fetch` now follows the Web level: at Cautious (the default) a fetch to a host you have not allowed asks, where it used to run. `--allow Fetch` or `--policy web=permissive` keeps every host running. "Always allow" on a fetch now writes `host:<host>` instead of `Fetch`, so it never allows every URL.
- Headless `cn -p` and `cn serve` keep running fetches to public hosts in this release, and print one line on standard error at the first such fetch. The switch to following your Web level moves from 2.36 to 2.38: from 2.38 a headless fetch follows your Web level, so at Cautious only hosts you allowed run.
- A fetch to a domain in `trustedDomains` now runs without asking at Cautious and Automatic, where it used to ask. While the list is set, every other host still asks.
- A fetch to a cloud metadata service (`169.254.169.254`, `fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`, `metadata.google.internal`, `metadata.goog`, in any spelling, or a name that resolves to one) is now refused at every level, IDGAF included, as the start URL and at every redirect. It used to ask, like other private addresses. A URL with a user name or password in it is now refused by the permission layer too, as the fetch already did.
- At IDGAF, your own `floor:` rules now bind on web fetches, alongside the fetch's built-in safety checks. A web fetch keeps its own hard checks, and the policy files stay locked.
- At IDGAF, the other safety checks stay off until you turn them on. A secret read followed by a network call, a push or a publish runs at IDGAF. In 2.34.0 that call was the one IDGAF refused. Turn the shield on and that call is refused again, and is never asked. With safety checks off, or with `protect-secrets` off, it runs at the other levels too.

### Fixes

- Choosing "Read it for this model" after a reply leaked a tool call now writes `toolDialect` on a model that is only a `from:` catalog reference. It used to say the config could not be edited, because the save looked for a `name` the entry does not have.

### Upgrade notes

- **Headless fetch.** `cn -p` and `cn serve` still fetch public hosts. The notice names 2.38 as the release where a headless fetch follows your Web level. To keep every host running after that, use `--allow Fetch` or `--policy web=permissive`, or allow the domains in `permissions.yaml`.
- **Web level.** Until you set `levels.web`, Web follows Tool use. Interactive `cn` at Cautious now asks before fetching a host you have not allowed.
- **IDGAF and safety checks.** Leave `safetyChecks` unset and IDGAF runs the calls 2.34.0 refused after a secret was read. Set `safetyChecks: on` to refuse that call at IDGAF again. The shield writes the same key.
- **Firewalls and sandboxes.** No new host.
